Maintenance Report — MNT-0187-007

Asset: WELL-0187 (NE-08 Well 187, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 29 Mar 2024 08:00 · Finished: 30 Mar 2024 10:00 · Well stopped for this job: 26 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0187-0075 on 2024-03-28 Report written: 01 Apr 2024

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0187-0075 at 12:30 on 2024-03-28 found crude oil on the pad: about 9.5% of the pad area, estimated 2.9 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 1.9 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Cleaned free oil out of the cellar.
  2. Unbolted the flange and removed the failed gasket.
  3. Fitted a new gasket and new bolts, torqued to specification.
  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 290 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 232 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.3 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0187-007 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.3% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Parts and cost

ItemUSD
Flange gasket and bolts745
Absorbents and berms1,491
Soil hauling and disposal2,733
Labour (company crew)5,983
Total10,952

Compliance check

WS-05MetTested at 1.25 × maximum operating pressure, held 4 hours

WS-07MetWritten 2 days after the work (limit 3 days)

Notes and recommendations

  • Inspect the remaining joints on this flowline.
  • Record the leak location for the flowline maintenance program (RC-05).

maintenance.action: Replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0187-011

Asset: WELL-0187 (NE-08 Well 187, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 26 Jul 2024 08:00 · Finished: 31 Jul 2024 01:00 · Well stopped for this job: 113 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0187-0091 on 2024-07-25 Report written: 01 Aug 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0187-0091 showed the wellhead at 34.5 °C with the air at 34.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 3 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

Notes and recommendations

  • Clean the motor cooling fins at each scheduled service.
  • Summer heat raises the risk of motor trips on this field.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0187-022

Asset: WELL-0187 (NE-08 Well 187, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 18 Jul 2026 08:00 · Finished: 22 Jul 2026 01:00 · Well stopped for this job: 89 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0187-0190 on 2026-07-16 Report written: 23 Jul 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid stopped reaching the flowline and the rod load spiked on the downstroke. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0187-0190 showed the wellhead at 47.4 °C with the air at 38.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 2 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Sand and scale build-up in the pump barrel.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.

  • Send the old pump for teardown.

maintenance.action: Replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0187-023

Asset: WELL-0187 (NE-08 Well 187, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 08 Aug 2026 08:00 · Finished: 18 Aug 2026 17:00 · Well stopped for this job: 249 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0187-0193 on 2026-08-06 Report written: 19 Aug 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator found an oil puddle under the gearbox. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0187-0193 showed the wellhead at 36.0 °C with the air at 31.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 8 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Seal wear, made worse by heat and a low oil level.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0187-023 (WS-06).
